correctness.rationale: The three-term orthogonal basis (1,t,t²−1/q) has exact beta norms 1,1/q,2(q−1)/(q²(q+2)); this gives the displayed quadratic reproducing kernel and the integrated upper-tail step response F(z,a). For each cutoff a, maximizing the quadratic in z yields either z=1 or the interior vertex z=−1/((q+2)a), whose admissible range is a≤−1/(q+2). Independently refactoring K(1,a) and K(z*(a),a) gives critical thresholds u=1/(sqrt(q+3)+1) and v=−1/(sqrt(q+3)−1), and the only two global candidates E(q),I(q). At endpoint a=−1 the response is 1; both candidate branch maxima exceed 1 on the domain. The positive Stieltjes-mixture representation extends the sharp step bound to every bounded nondecreasing f. Reflection gives the lower envelope, with both stated equality cases and ties. q↓1 weight and q=3 radical limits have consistent beta-tail behavior. Independent SymPy identities verify both factorizations, and sampled high-precision quadrature across eight positive q values agrees with the analytic branch envelope; finite samples are not the all-q proof.
residual_risks: The beta-tail comparison does not prove a unique weight-parameter branch crossing; the final claim explicitly does not assert it.

value.rationale: A natural finite-degree orthogonal spectral projector applied to monotone [0,1]-valued data need not preserve range; the exact worst overshoot controls amplitude safety and identifies all sharp cutoff/evaluation pairs. The two competing geometry branches and switch with the Jacobi weight are a mathematically meaningful classification rather than routine asymptotic Gibbs rephrasing; the unproved uniqueness of the crossing is not needed for value.
residual_risks: Application is limited to symmetric Jacobi weights and degree two; no higher-degree or nonsymmetric classification.

limitations: Crossing set is exactly {q:E(q)=I(q)} but uniqueness and explicit crossing threshold are NOT claimed.
f is monotone and [0,1]-valued almost everywhere under symmetric beta measure, q>1 only.
